author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chicopee police said Tuesday that a Jeep involved in a weekend crash with an Agawam ambulance had fled an attempted traffic stop earlier that night.

Western Mass News reported that the ambulance was traveling on a mutual-aid call when the vehicles collided around 1:30 a.m. Saturday at Boland Way and East Columbus Avenue in Springfield. Two Agawam firefighter-paramedics were treated for minor injuries.

A passenger in the Jeep was ejected and taken to a hospital. Police said there were no reported serious injuries from the crash, though the passenger’s specific condition was not released. The Jeep’s driver, a Palmer man, was detained by Springfield police and transferred to Chicopee police.

Authorities said the driver faces multiple charges, but the station’s update did not provide the complete list or identify him. The allegations have not been proven in court. The new account clarifies the sequence before the collision while leaving questions about speed, impairment and the final crash reconstruction unanswered. The ambulance had been in service for less than a month.
dek: A new police account links the weekend Springfield crash to an earlier traffic stop; two paramedics suffered minor injuries.
headline: Police say Jeep fled Chicopee stop before striking Agawam ambulance
